title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to Grothendieck's sequel to La Longue Marche, 'variations on the loop equation'. Write \hat\pi_{0,3} for the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,\infty}. It is free profinite on the loops l_0 and l_1, and its centre is trivial. M_{0,3}^{!~} is a group of 'special' automorphisms (or outer-automorphism lifts) of \hat\pi_{0,3}. Each such automorphism u_{\alpha,\beta} is determined by a pair (\alpha,\beta) of elements of \hat\pi_{0,3}, which conjugate l_0 and l_1, roughly u_{\alpha,\beta}(l_0) ~ \alpha l_0^\lambda \alpha^{-1} and u_{\alpha,\beta}(l_1) ~ \beta l_1^\lambda \beta^{-1}. The group S_0 M_{0,3}^{!~} consists of pairs (u,f), with u an automorphism and f in \hat\pi_{0,3}, such that int(f)\circ u = u_{\alpha,\beta} is special. Equivalently, its elements are triples (\alpha,\beta,f).

Step 1: the inner part. The triples (1,1,f) are the pairs with int(f)u = id, i.e. u = int(f)^{-1}. Because the centre is trivial, they form a subgroup isomorphic to \hat\pi_{0,3}. The section is (32): f \mapsto (int(f)^{-1}, f).

Step 2: semidirect product (31). S_0 M^{!~} \simeq M^{!~}[0] \ltimes \hat\pi_{0,3}. Here M^{!~}[0] is a normalised subgroup of M^{!~} (presumably the elements with trivial f-part). It acts on \hat\pi_{0,3} tautologically, via M^{!~}[0] \subset M^{!~} \subset Aut(\hat\pi_{0,3}). This is the standard splitting of the 'holomorph-like' group of pairs (automorphism, group element).

Step 3: the canonical \hat Z. The pairs (u,f) = (1, l_0^n) satisfy fu = int(l_0^n). Since int(l_0^n) fixes l_0 and conjugates l_1 by l_0^n, one gets \alpha = \beta = l_0^n, up to the normalisation of \alpha modulo the centraliser l_0^{\hat Z}. Hence (33): n \mapsto (l_0^n, l_0^n, l_0^n).

Step 4 (next page). The composition law (34) is u'' = u'u, \alpha'' = u'(\alpha)\alpha', \beta'' = u'(\beta)\beta', f'' = u'(f)f'. This is a cocycle-type law of the same shape as Ihara's and Drinfeld's composition law in GT, (\lambda_1,f_1)(\lambda_2,f_2) = (\lambda_1\lambda_2, f_1\cdot F_1(f_2)).

Purpose. The construction is then transported to the groups SM_{\rho,\sigma} = SG^*_{\rho,\sigma} \ltimes G, defined via the homomorphism \Theta. These are towers of groups built from the (\alpha,\beta,\mu,\varepsilon) data of the 'loop equation', a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type setting.
errors: Internal convention clash. The text says the subgroup of triples (1,1,f) corresponds to the couples (int(f)^{-1}, f), i.e. fu = u_{\alpha,\beta}. Yet (32) sends f \mapsto (int(f)^{-1}, f) \leftrightarrow (1,1,f^{-1}). The next page writes elements as f^{-1}u_{\alpha,\beta} and explicitly remarks 'identification au passage de f_* et f^{-1} !'. So the f vs f^{-1} convention is not yet stabilised on this page; it is harmless but inconsistent.
The label (31) is reused: the previous page already has an equation (31). This is a numbering slip.
\alpha = l_0^n is forced only after a normalisation of \alpha modulo the centraliser of l_0 (which is l_0^{\hat Z}). This normalisation is left implicit here.

ideas.what: The group S_0M^{!~}_{0,3} of pairs (automorphism u, element f) with int(f)u special, and its splitting as M^{!~}[0] \ltimes \hat\pi_{0,3}.
ideas.modern_name: Lift of an outer-automorphism subgroup to Aut of a centre-free group; holomorph-type semidirect product; GT-type groups acting on \hat F_2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard group theory; in the GT context Ihara (1980s–1990) and Drinfeld (1990)
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or the published Longue Marche excerpts as far as known (unsure)

ideas.what: The canonical subgroup \hat Z = <l_0> embedded as n \mapsto (l_0^n, l_0^n, l_0^n).
ideas.modern_name: Inertia/local monodromy at 0 inside the arithmetic-geometric fundamental-group extension
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (inertia subgroups in Galois actions on \hat\pi_1 of P^1 minus 3 points)

ideas.what: Composition law \alpha'' = u'(\alpha)\alpha', f'' = u'(f)f' for triples (\alpha,\beta,f) (completed on the next page).
ideas.modern_name: Composition law in GT / the Ihara monoid

missed.claim: Historical rather than mathematical. Grothendieck is here building, in his own (\alpha,\beta,f) parametrisation, the semidirect-product and composition-law formalism for a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group acting on \hat\pi_{0,3}. This formalism is usually attributed to Ihara and Drinfeld. The page itself contains only routine group theory, but it documents the independent development of this formalism in the 'loop equation' notes.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is relevant to the history and priority of GT-type constructions. The dating ('s.d.') would need to be fixed to make any priority claim.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine semidirect-product bookkeeping and identification of an inertia \hat Z. It is of interest mainly as evidence of Grothendieck's private GT-type formalism; no new mathematical result appears on the page.
transcription_corrections: The subscript on Aut in the inclusion M^{!~}[0] \subset M^{!~} \subset Aut_?(\hat\pi_{0,3}) is unclear. It looks like a short underlined abbreviation (possibly 'ext' or 'loc'); the reading is uncertain.
In (32) the struck-out letter before int(f)^{-1} is indeed an 'f'. The resulting expression is (int(f)^{-1}, f) \leftrightarrow (1,1,f^{-1}).
(33) reads: \hat Z \to S_0 M_{0,3}^{!~} s'identifie à n \mapsto (\alpha = l_0^n, \beta = l_0^n, f = l_0^n).
The top-margin '495' is Grothendieck's own page number; '387' at the bottom is the archive folio.
